data.body:
## Stood down on the scanner blocker -- another session owns it

The operator reports the session responsible for the broken scanner job is investigating. Stopped my
agent (it had reached plan-review but had NOT claimed anything, so 90c7 remains open with no
assignee -- nothing of mine blocks them). Marked the task complete on my side and handed the findings
over on the ticket rather than discarding them. 90c7 may be a duplicate of that session's own record
(change 2595 / ticket aa9e); theirs to merge or close.

TWO CORRECTIONS I OWE, both from operator pushback, and the second is the more instructive:

1. 'The problem is NOT asymmetry. If it was, a rebase would fix it.' Correct, and the disconfirming
   evidence was already in my own brief -- change 2607 was branched from 6125c5345f01 ITSELF, the
   commit that added the workflow, and still fails. I wrote that fact down and then kept a label that
   it contradicts. The failure mode is worth naming: I recorded the counter-evidence as a caveat
   ('stale base is not sufficient') instead of letting it kill the hypothesis. A caveat that
   contradicts the headline IS a refutation; parking it as a footnote is how a wrong frame survives.

2. 'Check whether the scheduled CI is failing on main.' The right next question, and it exposed that
   I had never established the base rate. Findings: test.yml is the branch-head lane, deliberately
   EXCLUDED from push-on-main (its concurrency group cancels in-progress runs, and on main github.ref
   is the constant refs/heads/main, so every push cancelled its predecessor and rendered a healthy
   main as a trail of red X's) -- so branch health comes from a ~6-hourly SCHEDULE. The last
   scheduled run (33824556786, 01:07) PREDATES the scanner merge (03:37) and contains no scanner job,
   so it could not answer the question at all. Dispatched test.yml against main manually
   (run 33839813271) to get the answer rather than wait ~6 hours.

THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING, which came out of checking rather than theorising: the scanner job NEVER
RAN BEFORE MERGE. Change 2595's own Verified run (33831682168) has 26 jobs -- lint, typecheck, four
pytest cells, artifact-probe, optionality, mutation shards, eval-discipline, pip-audit, golden-path,
sandbox enforcement -- and NO scanner-integration job. It was granted Verified +1 without that job
ever executing. So the escape is not 'validated under conditions that did not match' but 'never
validated at all'. That is a sharper and more checkable property, and it reframes the prevention
question from 'detect divergence between lanes' to 'a newly added CI job must actually EXECUTE on the
change that introduces it, or its Verified vote is vacuous'. Handed to the owning session.

ALSO CONFIRMED: 9a17 fails on MAIN itself, not just patchsets -- the 01:07 scheduled run failed on
pytest py3.13 and sweep (windows). Since branch health only refreshes ~6-hourly, a defect like this
degrades main's health signal for up to six hours before it is even visible. Recorded on 9a17.

2600's merge conflict: already resolved locally and merely unpushed. Gerrit's patchset 2 (921452107d5e)
has parent 08a39c39c50d, several commits behind main; the worktree HEAD (4540c0905ff4) has merge-base
= 6125c5345f01, 0 commits behind, merge-tree CLEAN, Change-Id intact. The agent had already hit and
resolved the real conflict -- Makefile .PHONY, where main added 'scanner-integration' and 2600 added
'e2e-deps' -- by keeping both. Told it to fold its uncommitted remediation into the commit and push,
with the reminder that make amend-msg touches the MESSAGE ONLY and 'git show --stat HEAD' is the
check.
